problem.title: Additivity of classical capacity and related problems

question.summary: The source asked to prove that the Holevo quantity is additive for every pair of quantum channels or to give an explicit counterexample. Hastings' random-unitary counterexample, combined with Shor's equivalences, showed that additivity fails.
question.importance: Additivity would have collapsed the regularised expression for the classical capacity of every quantum channel into a clean single-letter Holevo formula, and it was known to be equivalent to additivity of minimal output entropy, additivity and strong superadditivity of the entanglement of formation, and p-norm multiplicativity near p = 1.

targetClauses.label: Additivity of the Holevo capacity
targetClauses.text: The archived statement asks to prove that the Holevo quantity satisfies chi(T1 tensor T2) = chi(T1) + chi(T2) for every pair of quantum channels, or else to give an explicit counterexample.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: A general proof of the additivity identity, or a pair of channels for which it fails.

claims.title: Hastings disproves additivity of the Holevo capacity
claims.text: Hastings produced random-unitary channels in very large dimension that violate additivity of the minimal output von Neumann entropy. Via Shor's equivalence this directly implies failure of additivity of the Holevo capacity chi and of superadditivity of the entanglement of formation, so the archived additivity conjecture is false and the classical capacity is not given by a single-letter Holevo formula.

evidence.sourceLocator: Main result: random-unitary channels with a strict minimal-output-entropy gap
evidence.label: Nature Physics

decisions.rationale: Hastings' peer-reviewed counterexample, transferred by Shor's peer-reviewed equivalence theorem, refutes the universal additivity identity stated in the archived problem.

cautions.label: Scope
cautions.text: Additivity of chi still holds for special classes (identity channel, unital qubit channels, the depolarising channel in every dimension, entanglement-breaking channels, and some Gaussian cases); quantitative sub-questions such as the size of the violation, the qubit-channel case and the rate of convergence of the regularisation remain open.
